C-WINDOWS-SAVE-PIPELINE.Name: Windows save pipeline: the file.save command executes but the disk write never completes
C-WINDOWS-SAVE-PIPELINE.Summary: On the Windows polygon the save command runs but does not persist: with a document open from disk and a dirty buffer (isSaved false), executing file.save — via the rescued Ctrl+Alt+S-era accelerator, via the mt::menu-invoked event dispatch, or via Ctrl+S — leaves isSaved false and the file's size/mtime unchanged. The untitled-tab path behaves correctly (a native Save File dialog opens), so the command layer and the accelerator dispatcher are healthy; the breakdown sits somewhere between the renderer save flow and the Rust write (mt::save-file IPC or its plumbing). macOS saves normally and the e2e suite mocks the IPC, so CI stays green. This spec is the root-cause investigation and fix for the Windows write path.
C-WINDOWS-SAVE-PIPELINE.ApprovalBasis: Owner decision via the interactive menu 2026-11-01 («Фикс save-бага: в 2.9.0 или следующим поездом?» answered «Чинить в 2.9.0 (рекомендую)») after the root cause was presented in chat with the fix sizing (~15 lines in check_path, guards intact). Covers authoring, implementation and train admission; the release boundaries stay owner-controlled.
C-WINDOWS-SAVE-PIPELINE.AppliedEvidence: b2ed67d9 (branch commit, safety-gated) -> PR #162 squash-merge f7ffccd8 into main 2026-11-01 (owner menu decision); gates: m010_security 29/29, m001_save_close 16/16, grace final 2/2, full PR checks green; polygon disk-write proof on the rebuilt NSIS (real Ctrl+S: isSaved true, mtime moved, content round-trips). Admitted to the 2.9.x-next train as userFacing item #12.
C-WINDOWS-SAVE-PIPELINE.ProblemEvidence: 2026-11-01 polygon round on the fixed build (NSIS from 42085791, workspace D:\_prj\simen\LoanLossProvisions-xron): (1) tab focused on D:\_prj\simen\LoanLossProvisions-xron\README.md, buffer dirtied via editor insertText — pinia reports saved=false with the edit in the markdown tail; (2) real SendInput Ctrl+S (cua hotkey, foreground) — the dispatcher marker BLOCK_ACCELERATOR_FIRED chord=Ctrl+S cmd=file.save fires, so the command executes; (3) after the save: saved stays false, file mtime stays 2026-03-26 00:06, size unchanged, probe text absent from disk; repeated with the dialogs dismissed and the correct tab focused — same outcome; (4) the untitled tab correctly opens the native Save File dialog on Ctrl+S; (5) no save-related errors surface in the webview console during the failing save. Prior art: the 2026-10-30 pilot already noted "typed text never reached disk (no autosave)" — consistent with a write path that silently does nothing on Windows. ROOT CAUSE (2026-11-01 evening, notification-stack read + code walk): the failure is NOT silent — the renderer's notification stack carries `Save failure / IpcError { code: "MT_FS_PATH_DENIED", message: "path traversal: D:\_prj\simen\LoanLossProvisions-xron\README.md resolves outside sandbox \"", command: "mt::fs::write" }`. m010_security::check_path compares the request against the sandbox purely LEXICALLY/COMPONENT-WISE: the permissive default sandbox "/" (SecurityCtx::default) normalizes on Windows to a root-only path "\", and a DOS path D:\... carries a Prefix(D:) component that never starts_with a bare root — so with the default sandbox EVERY absolute write on Windows is denied (on POSIX "/" prefixes every absolute path, which is why macOS saves). Second layer of the same disease: when a workspace IS restored, m005_prefs::workspace_set_inner stores fs::canonicalize output — on Windows the \\?\ UNC device form — which the renderer's DOS-form request can never prefix-match either.

Goals.Goal: Make m010_security::check_path Windows-honest without weakening any guard: a root-only sandbox (the permissive "/" default) admits absolute paths on every platform, and both sides of the prefix comparison are compared with the \\?\ / \\?\UNC\ device prefixes stripped — NUL/overlong checks, lexical ..-normalization, symlink resolution and prefix denial outside the sandbox all keep holding (a \\?\C:\other request against a D:\ sandbox stays denied).

Fix the write path so saving a dirty, path-backed document on Windows persists the buffer to disk (isSaved returns true, size/mtime move, content round-trips) through every trigger: keyboard accelerator, ☰ menu, and command palette.

Extend the verification surface so this cannot regress silently again: at least one non-mocked proof that the save IPC performs a real write on the Windows platform (polygon scenario or a Windows CI lane), since the macOS e2e mocks the IPC today.

Constraints.Constraint: macOS behavior is the reference and must not change; the fix targets the Windows (and, if shared, Linux) write path.
No new command ids and no changes to the autosave/dirty-detection semantics beyond what the root cause requires.
The polygon workspace belongs to the owner (D:\_prj\simen\...) — disk probes there are read-only; dirty-buffer and write proofs use a scratch document in D:\polygon.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No redesign of the save flow, autosave, or the untitled-tab Save As dialog (that path works).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The failing stage is identified with evidence (marker, log, or IPC trace) — not inferred from absence; the fix lands with a regression test pinning that stage.
Polygon acceptance on the fixed build: a dirty scratch document under D:\polygon saves via Ctrl+S (mtime moves, content round-trips, isSaved true) and via the ☰ menu path.
macOS e2e and unit suites stay green unchanged.

AffectedAreas.Area: TBD at root-cause: candidates are src/renderer/src/store/editor.js (save flow), src/renderer/src/_shims/install-window-globals.js (ipc mapping), src-tauri save command implementation, tests. Graph/verification anchors assigned with the plan.

VerificationIntent.Command: TBD — polygon scratch-doc save round (real SendInput + mtime + content) plus the relevant unit/e2e suites once the failing stage is known.

Assumptions.Assumption: The bug reproduces on 2.9.0-train builds generally (observed on main 388b6669 and on the fixed branch build), i.e. it predates C-WINDOWS-MENU-ACCELERATORS.
The execCommand-based dirtying reliably marks the buffer dirty (pinia showed saved=false) — the failure is downstream of dirty detection.
